subject: Dedicated capacity ask: context cache fingerprint, tiling strategy & quantization impact

Subject: Dedicated capacity — rough memory needs and timeline

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to get a concrete sizing request so we can fast-track engineering approvals. High level: we expect ~1200 concurrent inference sessions at peak for a 16k-context model and ~300 for 64k-context (rare). Typical prompt + response averages 5.5k tokens.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provide a memory "fingerprint" (per-model, per-context) that factors KV cache tiling/replication and expected per-request on-GPU footprint for int8 vs bfloat16?
- What committed GPU count would you recommend for a 1yr reserved pool with a 99th pct latency SLO of 250ms for interactive flows?

I've attached a mapping table that shows our traffic patterns by route and a draft SOW. We'll need the numbers by Wednesday EOD to include in our procurement packet.

Attachments: noventia-mapping-table.xlsx, SOW_draft_v2.docx

Best,

From: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — rough memory needs and timeline

Hi Sana — thanks for the workbook and the SOW. High level reply while we prepare a detailed table:

1) Memory fingerprint concept: we compute an empirical per-session GPU working set that includes model param residency, transient KV cache (sharded or replicated depending on pod tiling), and temporary tensors for decoding. We provide two fingerprints: steady-state (incoming prompt + KV) and tail-case (full 64k context + long generation).

2) Quant families: int8 dynamic quant gives ~2.6–3x reduction in param memory vs bfloat16 with small perf variability; int4 can save more but increases decoding latency variance. For KV cache the savings are roughly proportional (so an int8 KV cache reduces KV footprint by ~3x).

3) Pod tiling: for your concurrency mix we typically recommend mix of 1) shared pools for 16k-fast routes (continuous batching) and 2) isolated pods for 64k long-context jobs (to avoid KV thrash). That affects replication: 64k shards are often 1:1 on dedicated pods; 16k can be sharded 2–4x across replicas to increase throughput.

I'll have Marcus and Priyom run the workbook through our capacity planner and return a model-by-model table with committed GPU recommendations by EOD Wednesday.

Quick ask: can you confirm percent of requests that are latency-sensitive (web UI) vs batch/async? That lets us split reserved pool vs burst capacity.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Forwarding internal sizing notes and a short table summary (attached PDF). Key technical points below.

---
From: Marcus Lin (internal sizing notes)
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 08:38

Team — I ran Noventia's mapping through our planner. Assumptions and results:
- Model baseline: 70B param dense model (fp16/bfloat16 baseline) -> param residency ~140GB across sharded devices (model offloading not desired for latency-sensitive flows).
- KV cache cost: 16k context = ~12GB per 1000 concurrent sessions on GPU in bfloat16 KV form; int8 reduces that KV to ~4GB/1000 concurrent sessions.
- Tiling: with a 4-way shard (pod tiling) we can support higher concurrent sessions per GPU for 16k routes due to reduced per-instance KV residency; however replication factor for 64k routes needs to be higher to avoid cross-pod KV fetchs that spike latency.
- Suggested committed pool (for interactive 99th pct 250ms):
  * Scenario A (bfloat16 baseline): 48 x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (reserved) + 8 GPU burst buffer
  * Scenario B (int8-safe quant path for model + KV): 18 x A100-80GB equiv (or 36 x A100-40GB equiv) + 6 GPU burst
- Notes on safety: int8 quant requires calibration/eval on Noventia prompts; we estimate a ~6–9% throughput boost on top of memory savings due to cache locality improvements but must run prompt-quality regressions.

Attachments referenced: redwood-kv-footprint.pdf (tables), internal-runbook link (HubSpot:HS-4582)

Action items: Priyom to produce the table per model variant (16k/32k/64k) and to enumerate test plan steps for quant QA.

Marcus

Hi Sana — attaching the fingerprint PDF and an initial committed-pool recommendation. Summary here for the procurement packet:

- Per-model fingerprints attached (redwood-kv-footprint.pdf) showing steady-state and tail-case memory per concurrent session for 16k/32k/64k.
- Recommended reserved commitment (conservative / quant-path):
  * Conservative (bfloat16): 48 x A100-80GB equiv for reserved pool to meet 99th pct 250ms; add 8 GPU burst capacity for spikes.
  * Optimized (int8 after QA): 18 x A100-80GB equiv reserved + 6 GPU burst. We recommend a phased approach: reserve conservative capacity for Q1 of the contract while running the quant QA bench on a separate non-reserved test pool; switch 35–40% of steady traffic to quantized model variants during Q2 once quality gates pass.

- MAP / timeline:
  1) Today: Redwood provides fingerprint PDF and cost delta. (attached)
  2) Wed (EOD): Procurement includes conservative estimate in packet.
  3) Week 2: Redwood-run quant QA (prompt set + eval) and a 2-week canary with 5% traffic.
  4) Week 6: Review canary, expand to 40% quant traffic and update reserved counts if validated.

Attachments: redwood-kv-footprint.pdf, SOW_draft_v2.docx

Next step — Sana, confirm latency-sensitive % split and preferred contract start date and we will finalize the SOW numbers.

Thanks,
